families.name: B — recovery backfill, gap arithmetic collapsed to zero
families.mechanism: Same physical event as family A, seen through the arithmetic anchor rather than the read anchor. Each row's claim-level anchor is `a - b` with a = len:$.candidates of the cell's candidate_manifest.json and b = len:$.results of its probabilities.json — the document's own gap definition (line 61: `gap = expected_input - len(probabilities.results)`). Operand-by-operand: the manifest operand `a` is UNCHANGED era-to-now in all 12 rows (2840/2840, 3601/3601, 572/572, 572/572, 802/802, 1114/1114, 3601/3601, 802/802, 802/802, 1114/1114, 4358/4358, 572/572 — moved=False in every case), while the probabilities operand `b` grew by exactly the quoted gap and landed on the manifest count. Hence current gap == 0 for all 12 rows (verified: every arithmetic row's `actual` is 0.0). The systematic offset is therefore precisely quoted_gap → 0, with the whole movement carried by operand b. Note that the two 460-rows (046#26[0], 046#28[0]) and 046#14[2] are three separate prose restatements of the same single cell figure (image-t0.0/verified-v1-n10), and 046#17[1]/046#31[5] are two restatements of the h8-v2/wbf/scale-4 gap of 15 — same mechanism, same cell, so no independent verification burden beyond the one cell each.

Two rows — 046#37[0] (quoted 57) and 046#39[0] (quoted 1) — sit in the 2026-05-06 annotation section, whose text is absent from the 2026-05-03 blob; they were resolved at d78601b62 instead, and are era-faithful there (gap 57 and gap 1 still stood when that annotation was written, at 11:03 +0800; the closure commit 6683952ac landed at 16:38 +0800 the same day, five and a half hours later, and is a descendant of d78601b62 by merge-base). row_level_exceptions.mechanism: The verbatim span is line 591-593: 'its 460-candidate gap (57% of the input pool) is large enough that recovery may shift its F1 / MCC rankings appreciably.' Value index 1 is correctly typed in the extraction as kind 'percentage' with quantity 'gap as a share of the input candidate pool', but it carries no per-value `method` or `path`, so it silently inherits the claim-level anchor `a - b`, which yields a count of CANDIDATES, not a share. The comparer therefore measured a percentage against a candidate count. The document is arithmetically correct at its era: 460/802 = 57.36%, which presents as '57%'. My era re-resolution reproduces the defect's signature — the expression returns 460 at adf95dbf9 against a quoted 57, the only ERA-DIVERGE result in the partition — and that is exactly the false DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA signal this class of extraction error manufactures.
row_level_exceptions.why_not_snapshot_divergence: The primary MISMATCH verdict (57 vs 0) happens to be directionally right by coincidence, because the current gap is 0 candidates AND the current share is also 0%. But the comparison is not unit-commensurable, the recorded abs_error of 57 is meaningless, and the era axis is inverted. The defect must be repaired in the extraction before the row can be dispositioned on evidence rather than luck.
row_level_exceptions.evidence_of_extractor_convention_breach: The extractor's own convention within this same batch is to mark values that the claim anchor cannot derive with `method: "anchor-unknown"` — it did so for 046#14 values 0 and 1, and for 046#31 values 0 through 4, leaving only the anchor-derivable value inheriting the arithmetic method. It failed to apply that convention to 046#28 value 1.
row_level_exceptions.repair: Set 046#28 value 1 `method` to 'anchor-unknown', OR give it a per-value expression `100*(a-b)/a` over the existing operands. Under the second repair the row re-derives as era 57.36% vs current 0.0%, i.e. it joins family B as a SNAPSHOT-DIVERGENCE. Document unchanged either way.
row_level_exceptions.document_status: The source document is correct at its era and needs no repair for this row.

escalations.kind: INSTRUMENT — era_check resolves at the wrong era for banner-carrying historical documents
escalations.severity: high (process); zero disposition change within my partition
escalations.finding: scripts/recompute_c4_claims.py:238-255 `find_era_commit` selects the newest commit whose tree holds the extraction's recorded blob of the source document. For any historical document that has since received a superseded-figures banner or an appended annotation — which is precisely what ruling 1 MANDATES for this document class — the recorded blob is the post-banner blob, so the 'era' resolved is the banner-edit date, not the era of the claims. Here the extraction blob 6f2ceb7ad30c first appears at 5d91c2a97a73 (2026-08-01), three months after the body (adf95dbf9, 2026-05-03) and after every recovery commit. Consequence: era_check reported `faithful: false` for all 43 of my rows, when 42 are era-faithful on re-resolution at the true era.
escalations.blast_radius: All 110 MISMATCH rows in c4-recompute-report.json whose source_file is this document carry era_check.commit == 5d91c2a97a73 and faithful == false: 67 in batch 043, 27 in batch 045, 16 in batch 046. My partition holds 43 of them; the remaining 67 (batch 043) belong to another partition and are exposed to the same false signal. Report-wide, 136 of 222 MISMATCH rows carry era_check.faithful == false across 7 source documents; reports/results-summary-session-58.md (15 rows) has the same structural exposure — first commit 8b596c00d 2026-03-26, last commit a6f58d1b7 2026-08-02.
escalations.why_this_matters: Ruling 14 makes per-claim era-faithfulness THE deciding axis and demotes the dated filename to advisory. A triager who trusts era_check.faithful==false here would land 42 era-faithful rows as DOC-DEFECT-AT-ERA — the exact inversion ruling 14 was written to prevent, arriving through the machinery ruling 14 relies on. The banner policy (ruling 1) and the era machinery (ruling 12) interact adversely: applying the banner is what breaks the era resolution.
escalations.recommended_fix: Make era-commit selection content-aware rather than blob-aware: resolve each claim at the newest commit whose blob still contains the claim's verbatim span (falling back to the first commit introducing the source document). That single change handles both failure modes seen here — the post-hoc banner AND the within-file multi-era case (my 046#37[0] and 046#39[0] correctly resolve to d78601b62, not adf95dbf9, under a span-presence rule). Until fixed, era_check on banner-carrying documents should be suppressed or explicitly labelled unreliable rather than emitted as `faithful: false`.
escalations.action_requested: PI decision on (a) whether to re-run era_check under a span-presence rule before GATE 3, and (b) notifying the partition holding batch 043's 67 rows on this document that their era_check field is unreliable.
